text:
sarah: heads-up: ECC spike on gpu-az3-41, seeing 4 Xid/CCE errors in 2m, pods started failing checkpoints
ben: thanks — are these persistent across reboots or appeared after the last driver update?
infra-bot: Alert: gpu-health:ecc_spike detected on gpu-az3-41 (4 events, 2m). Auto-probe scheduled at +30s.
kai: looks like a pattern after the 2026-03-01 driver roll, but we haven't seen cluster-wide noise. could be a flaky card.
sarah: pods on that node were on a k8s nodepool with mixed-burst. We need an automated flow that soft-cordons first, runs a memtest probe, and only escalates to drain if probe fails or Xid rate stays high.
leah: +1. Current autodrain is aggressive for single-signal spikes. It increases task churn and costs. We should do multi-signal aggregation: ECC + Xid + power/temp anomalies.
ben: proposal: policy engine with 3 buckets: transient (soft-cordon + probe), persistent (soft-drain->repair ticket), critical (immediate hard-drain if GPU panics or ECC > 100/min). Hysteresis: require 2 probes failing within 20m to mark persistent.
infra-bot: New workflow created: gpu-probe-orch v1.2 — runs memtest86+ via remote job, collects nvml logs, and tags node with gpu-probe:in-progress.
oncall-aaron: how do we prevent cascade in busy regions? evicting many pods in eu-west2 could starve latency pools. Need region-aware backoff and capacity reservation.
kai: agree. Add region_quota check and preferred fallback routing to ded-only pool. If quota < 10% free, postpone hard-drain for 15m and notify SRE.
sarah: also add a rapid-sample KV cache flush and model-serving sticky routing so active sessions aren't lost during soft-cordon.
ben: we should keep a short-lived warm pool to absorb evictions; cost impact ~2% on steady state. I'll model it.
leah: tests: simulate Xid burst + memtest failure, ensure orchestrator soft-cordons, runs probe, and after 2 failed probes within 15m it creates a repair ticket and hard-drains. Add e2e playbook.
kai: implementation notes: use taint: gpu-health=quarantine:NoSchedule for soft-cordon. probe job runs with hostPID, mounts /var/log/nvidia, runs nvdiag container, and returns probe_status in node annotation.
oncall-aaron: we should also wire this into oncall runbook: if probe fails and node is in critical pool, oncall gets page; otherwise notify channel with :warning:.
infra-bot: Test alert: synthetic Xid spike injected on test-gpu-node-7 at 2033456700. Orchestrator executed soft-cordon and probe succeeded (memtest 0/1 errors). No drain performed.
sarah: nice. test looks good. PR for orch here: https://git.redwood/infrapr/gpu-probe-orch/pulls/42 — includes metrics and PromQL for signal aggregation.
ben: action items: 1) add region_quota check (kai) 2) warm pool cost model (ben) 3) runbook updates & pages (oncall-aaron) 4) e2e tests in staging (leah). I'll open tickets.
leah: i'll schedule a dry-run next Tue 09:30 PT to exercise soft-cordon -> probe -> successful drain path in staging.
sarah: thanks all, let's keep the default behavior conservative. We can tighten thresholds once we have 48h of stable telemetry. :thumbsup:
